title: Accept every answer the text supports
statement: Accept every answer the text defensibly supports, and check that the hints and the reveal don't steer students toward only one of them.
example: One audited step accepted only one of two defensible actions.
detail: An external audit of four Grade 3 lessons found a step whose key accepted only one of two defensible actions, rejecting one that the story's next line follows directly, and a blank whose rubric accepted either of two characters while the reveal and the second hint steered only toward one. Both were still open in the register.

questions declare single- or multi-location demand; scoring accepts every defensible evidence set.

the reveal quotes the passage line byte-exact before stating the answer, or — where there is no single correct pick (a compare turn) — models one complete answer (pick + because + lesson word) rather than crowning a winner.

Scoring accepts any reason tied to a real clue in the passage rather than matching one exemplar sentence, and the accept-list is written from the clues, because Gygax and colleagues found no consensus even on texts designed to produce one agreed inference

even on texts designed to produce one agreed inference "there was no consensus. In fact some readers inferred emotions that were the precise opposite of that intended" (Kispal, quoting Gygax et al. 2004).

Second, single-correct motive items are riskier than they look, so the scoring of the child's written motive must accept any reason that is tied to a real clue, and the accept-list has to be written from the clues rather than from one exemplar sentence.

**Our L4 question is open by design** ("Tell me why you think she decided to go", rubric: "There is no single right reason"). The branches must therefore judge WHETHER a reason is given and grounded, never steer to one reason.
